forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. May 2 2026: no new credible AGI declaration. Backdrop: ARC-AGI-3 results (Mar 2026) show frontier models scoring <0.4% on a benchmark humans solve at 100%, reinforcing breadth-of-capability gaps. Frontier release cadence still compressing (median gap ~49 days in 2026 YTD). Hassabis and Amodei continue 'few years' AGI timelines, but no lab has formally declared AGI. Sequoia's January essay arguing 'long-horizon agents are functionally AGI' is investor commentary, not a credible-lab declaration. ~43 months to resolution.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Continued release-cadence compression to ~49 days median (+2pp)
Lab CEOs (Amodei, Hassabis) repeatedly anchoring public 'within a few years' timelines (+2pp)
Anthropic continuing to withhold next-generation Mythos 5 model citing capability concerns (+1pp)
$40B+ Google-Anthropic capital commitment signalling expectation of frontier-class capability (+1pp)
factors_down: ARC-AGI-3 March 2026 results: frontier models <0.4% vs 100% human (-4pp)
AGI definition still contested across labs and academia (-3pp)
Resolution window narrowing to <44 months (-2pp)
Capability gains still concentrated in narrow benchmarks rather than broad agentic deployment (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether withheld near-frontier models trigger a coordinated AGI declaration in 2026-27
Whether benchmark gains generalise to economically valuable agentic work over the next 18 months
Whether 3+ leading researchers coordinate on a public AGI declaration before 2030

update_triggers.up: Major lab publicly declares AGI; 3+ leading researchers endorse a specific milestone; ARC-AGI-3 saturated by frontier models
update_triggers.down: Stall in frontier capability gains; major labs walk back timelines; capex pullback or training-run cancellations

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Edge down 1pp to 19%. Latest data shows AI augmenting rather than displacing consultancy: UK consulting growth projected at 5.7% in 2026 and 7.4% in 2027 (MCA survey); 77% of UK firms have integrated AI. McKinsey's late-2025 cuts (~200 staff) targeted back-office functions, not consultant headcount; entry-level pyramids reshaping (LinkedIn: 25% of entry-level postings now require AI fluency, up from <5% two years ago) but revenue continues to grow. Global AI consulting market reached $11B in 2025 and is projected at $14B in 2026 (+26.5% CAGR), arguing for net revenue substitution toward AI-services lines rather than aggregate decline. Resolution requires ≥33% revenue or employment decline by end-2030 attributed by 2+ credible analyses primarily to AI — trend is in the wrong direction for YES.
forecasts.base_rate: ~15-20% — large industry contractions of ≥33% over a 5-6 year window are rare (historically 10-15% base rate); upward adjustment for AI-specific risk
factors_up: Entry-level analyst pyramid contraction visible in MBB hiring (+3pp)
AI agent capabilities continuing to compress research/synthesis tasks (+2pp)
Possibility of price compression as AI consulting deliverables commoditise (+1pp)
factors_down: UK consulting growth projected 5.7% in 2026, 7.4% in 2027 (-3pp)
AI consulting itself becoming a major revenue line (+26.5% CAGR) (-2pp)
Resolution requires ≥33% decline AND attribution to AI by 2+ analyses (-2pp)
Historical industry contractions of this magnitude over 5-6 years are rare (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether agentic AI displaces partner-level work, not just analyst tasks, before 2030
How quickly client willingness-to-pay for human consulting hours falls
Whether 'consultancy' is defined narrowly (strategy houses) or broadly (incl. tech/Big 4) at resolution

update_triggers.up: Big 4 or MBB announces ≥10% headcount cuts citing AI; consulting revenue contraction reported in two consecutive quarters; client willingness-to-pay surveys show sharp decline
update_triggers.down: Continued double-digit AI-services revenue growth; partner promotions resume at pre-2024 pace; client demand for human-led strategy work re-accelerates

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3%. Polling backdrop unchanged from April 30: Reform leads with a 6-point lead over Labour and Conservatives; Labour and Conservatives tied around 19% in Ipsos polling. Electoral Calculus seat projections: Reform on 266 seats, 197 ahead of Labour. May 7 2026 local elections expected to confirm severe Labour losses (forecasts of up to 74% of council seats lost). With ~3.5 years to a December-2029 deadline a recovery is mathematically possible, but every credible MRP, voting-intention and seat-projection model has Labour third or fourth in seats. Material upgrade requires either Reform implosion or Labour double-digit polling recovery — neither visible.
forecasts.base_rate: ~10% historical base rate for a governing party trailing third in mid-term polling and recovering to win most seats by next GE
factors_up: Local elections on May 7 could trigger leadership change and reset (+2pp)
~3.5 years remain until the December-2029 deadline (+1pp)
Reform is a young, untested party with execution risk (+1pp)
factors_down: Reform consistently leading every major poll for ~9 months (-3pp)
Labour and Conservatives tied at ~19%, far behind Reform (-3pp)
Electoral Calculus projecting Reform 266 seats, Labour 69 (-2pp)
MRP models continue to show Labour wipeout in marginals (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether the May 7 2026 local elections trigger a Labour leadership change
How Reform's vote translates into seats given FPTP dynamics
Whether Conservative-Reform vote consolidation or split shapes 2029 outcome

update_triggers.up: Labour reaches 28%+ in 3+ consecutive Westminster polls; Reform polling drops below 22%; major Reform scandal or split
update_triggers.down: Reform consolidates vote with Conservative defections; Labour leadership change without polling recovery; Labour falls below 18%

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 74%. With ~9 years to deadline, the probability remains dominated by trend extrapolation. Release cadence is still compressing (~49-day median frontier gap in 2026 YTD vs 170 days in 2023), and capex commitments (Google-Anthropic $40B, OpenAI Stargate-scale infrastructure) project frontier-scale training runs continuing through the late 2020s. ARC-AGI-3 results show breadth-of-capability gaps remain — but the question is about 2035, not 2030, giving substantially more time for these gaps to close. Lab CEOs continue to anchor 'within a decade' as a consensus public timeline.
factors_up: Release-cadence compression continuing in 2026 (+3pp)
Sustained frontier capex (>$200B/yr industry-wide) (+2pp)
Lab leadership consensus timelines clustered around 5-10 years (+2pp)
Multiple credible paths to AGI (scaling, agents, post-training, multi-modal) (+1pp)
factors_down: ARC-AGI-3 reveals significant remaining capability gaps (-3pp)
Definitional ambiguity could delay a credible AGI declaration (-2pp)
Historical AI hype cycles and prior 'AGI within a decade' predictions failing (-2pp)
Possible scaling laws plateau or compute-cost ceiling before 2030 (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether scaling continues to deliver capability gains through 2026-2030
Whether agentic capabilities generalise from narrow benchmarks to economically valuable work
Whether 3+ leading researchers will coordinate publicly on an AGI declaration

update_triggers.up: ARC-AGI-3 saturated; frontier model demonstrates broad agentic competence on novel domains; lab CEO formally declares AGI achieved
update_triggers.down: Two consecutive frontier releases without capability gains; capex retrenchment by major labs; major scaling-law failure published

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 10%. May 1 AEI China-Taiwan update confirms continued elevated tempo without crossing threshold: PLA Southern Theater Command surface task group exercising east of Luzon Strait (Apr 24); ~100 PRC coast guard/naval vessels deployed during KMT Chairperson Cheng's visit (up from baseline 50-60); live-fire drills in Yellow Sea; airspace restriction zone NE of Taiwan extended late-March to early-May. CSMonitor analysis (May 1) notes Beijing studying Iran's Strait of Hormuz blockade as a Taiwan playbook. Activity remains in 'pressure campaign / rehearsal' band, not a >72-hour blockade or assault. ~44 months to deadline.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5-7% base rate for major-power military blockades in a 4-year window absent prior conflict
factors_up: PLA exercise tempo and vessel deployments continuing to escalate above 2024 baseline (+2pp)
PRC explicitly studying Hormuz blockade dynamics for Taiwan application (+1pp)
Airspace restriction zones extending and becoming routine (+1pp)
Cross-strait political tension high after Taiwan presidential signalling (+1pp)
factors_down: Activity remains rehearsal/pressure rather than threshold-crossing (-3pp)
Taiwan domestic life largely normal per Al Jazeera reporting (-1pp)
Significant economic costs to Beijing from Taiwan blockade (~20% of global maritime trade through strait) (-2pp)
US-Japan-Philippines exercises (Balikatan 2026) continue to provide deterrence signal (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether a 'quarantine' or 'inspection' regime would meet the >72hr blockade threshold
How a Trump-administration crisis response would shape Beijing's risk calculation
Whether internal PRC economic pressure changes the political calendar

update_triggers.up: PLA conducts a >24hr maritime closure of Taiwan ports; explicit blockade announcement; mobilisation visible via OSINT
update_triggers.down: Cross-strait talks resume; reduction in vessel deployments; explicit PRC public statement de-escalating

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. Latest ONS data: CPI 3.3% YoY March 2026 (up from 3.0% in February); April 2026 release published Apr 22. PwC commentary and Bank of England April Monetary Policy Report indicate inflation persistence above target. With only 8 monthly readings remaining until the December 2026 print (last that could resolve before Jan 2027) and trajectory above 3%, falling 1.3+ percentage points to below 2.0% in a single month would be unprecedented absent a sharp recession or energy-price collapse. Effectively a tail-risk question now.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5% probability of a 130+bp CPI fall in 8 months absent a recession
factors_up: Possible energy-price reversal if global commodities soften (+1pp)
Possible base-effect oddity if a single category reverses sharply (+1pp)
Tail-risk recession scenario could compress headline CPI quickly (+1pp)
factors_down: March 2026 CPI 3.3%, trajectory higher not lower (-3pp)
BoE Monetary Policy Report flags inflation persistence (-2pp)
Services inflation remains sticky above 4% (-1pp)
Only 8 readings remain until resolution window closes (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether a sudden energy-price collapse could occur before end-2026
Whether a recession scenario materialises and pulls headline CPI down sharply
Whether ONS methodology changes could mechanically reduce the index

update_triggers.up: Two consecutive monthly CPI prints below 2.5%; sharp energy-price collapse; UK enters technical recession
update_triggers.down: CPI rises further above 3.5%; services inflation accelerates; BoE flags re-acceleration risk

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 97%. Marketing trajectory continues to be exceptional: trailer (released March 18) hit 718M views in 24 hours, surpassing Deadpool & Wolverine (365M, prior MCU record) within 8 hours and overall 24-hour record set by GTA VI. Confirmed July 31 2026 theatrical release leaves ~5 months of box office runway through Dec 31. Tom Holland Spider-Man precedent (No Way Home: $1.92B) and unprecedented trailer engagement signal demand far above the $1.5B threshold. Residual ~3% accounts for tail-risks (production setback, critical reception collapse, major exogenous event).
forecasts.base_rate: ~80% for a Tom Holland Spider-Man theatrical sequel exceeding $1.5B given franchise precedent
factors_up: Trailer set all-time 24-hour view record (718M, +5pp)
No Way Home precedent of $1.92B (+3pp)
Tom Holland headlining, Marvel Studios/Sony co-production model (+2pp)
5 months of runway after July 31 release (+2pp)
factors_down: Possible release-date slip (-1pp)
Critical reception risk for fourth Holland Spider-Man (-1pp)
Possible exogenous shocks affecting global box office (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether China release timing materially affects the 2026 cutoff
Whether competing tentpoles (e.g. Avatar 3) compress theatrical window
Whether word-of-mouth carries the run past the threshold by year-end

update_triggers.up: Pre-sales records broken at major chains; critic embargo lifts to >85% RT
update_triggers.down: Release date slip into 2027; major production issue disclosed; very poor early reviews

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. Latest credible reporting (April 2026): Anthropic at ~$30B ARR (Sacra, April 7), OpenAI at $25B+ ARR (The Information, late April; from $21.4B at end-2025). Combined as-reported: ~$55B already, with 8 months of growth runway and both companies on rapid trajectories (Anthropic +1,400% YoY; OpenAI +17% over four months). Even using OpenAI's preferred net-revenue accounting (which would revise Anthropic to ~$22B), combined would be ~$47B today and likely $65-80B by Dec 2026. Resolution allows 'most recent credible reporting' to include either method, and Bloomberg/FT/The Information have published the gross figures. Risk concentrated in growth deceleration in H2 2026.
forecasts.base_rate: ~90% for high-growth pair exceeding 1.27x combined ARR over 8 months given current trajectories
factors_up: Anthropic at $30B already, +1,400% YoY (+5pp)
OpenAI at $25B and accelerating (+3pp)
Combined ~$55B as-reported gives only 27% growth required to clear $70B (+3pp)
Q4 typically strongest enterprise booking quarter (+1pp)
factors_down: Growth deceleration risk if enterprise AI spend plateaus (-2pp)
OpenAI accounting dispute creates ambiguity in headline figures (-1pp)
Possible major model failure or trust event affecting both (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Which accounting method credible reporting will privilege at year-end
Whether Anthropic compute constraints throttle bookings
Whether enterprise AI spend slows in late 2026 macro slowdown

update_triggers.up: Either company posts a single quarter-over-quarter step-up; new enterprise contract leak >$5B
update_triggers.down: Either company reports flat or declining ARR for two consecutive months; major churn event disclosed

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 42%. OBR March 2026 EFO continues to forecast UK real GDP growth slowing from 1.4% in 2025 to 1.1% in 2026, then averaging 1.6% over the rest of the forecast (to ~2030). Per-person growth forecast averages 1.1% pa 2026-2030. November 2025 OBR revision cut medium-term productivity growth to 1.0% (from 1.3%). The OBR forecast straddles the 1.5% threshold for the first half of the 2030s, but a 10-year arithmetic mean above 1.5% requires recovery in the second half — depends materially on whether AI productivity gains land in the UK economy. IFS October 2025 outlook flagged 'narrow paths' to growth; KPMG December 2025 outlook remained cautious. With 4-year resolution window starting in 2030, probability sits near 50-50, modestly tilted below given current trend.
forecasts.base_rate: ~40% — historical UK 10-year averages above 1.5% are roughly even-money in 21st-century data
factors_up: OBR forecasting 1.6% average over forecast horizon (+5pp)
Possible AI productivity windfall arriving in late-2020s (+5pp)
Population growth still positive even with reduced migration (+2pp)
Long-term mean-reversion to 1.7-2.0% historic average (+2pp)
factors_down: OBR cutting medium-term productivity growth to 1.0% (-5pp)
Per-person growth forecast at only 1.1% pa (-3pp)
Population ageing reducing labour-supply growth to 0.5% by 2030 (-3pp)
Pre-financial-crisis 2% per-person growth has not returned for ~17 years (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers measurable UK productivity gains by mid-2030s
Whether net migration remains structurally lower
Whether the resolution definition treats unrevised vs revised ONS data

update_triggers.up: OBR revises medium-term productivity above 1.3%; UK net migration returns to 200k+; AI capex spillover begins to show in TFP data
update_triggers.down: Productivity growth revised below 0.8%; back-to-back recessions in 2027-2028; net migration negative for 2+ years
